cohort: Pregnant women who underwent cervical length measurements by transabdominal and transvaginal sonography between 20 and 29 gestational weeks.
finding: The study found that short cervical lengths (<2 cm) on transabdominal sonography had 100% sensitivity for predicting short cervical lengths on transvaginal sonography, suggesting that women with measurable and long cervical lengths on transabdominal sonography may not need transvaginal sonography for preterm birth prediction.
gest_age: 20-29 gestational weeks (for measurements), <34 gestational weeks (for preterm birth definition)
